senses.gloss: m. (תִּרְגֵּם) interpretation, translation, version, esp. Targum, the Chaldaic (Aramaic) versions of the Scriptures.
units: <cite ref="Megillah 3a:4">Meg. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>ת׳ של תורה וכ׳</he> the translation of the Torah was composed by Onkelos the proselyte from the mouth (by direction) of R. El. and R. Joshua; <he>ת׳ של נביאים וכ׳</he> the translation of the prophets was made by Jonathan ben Uzziel from the mouth of Haggai &c.
<cite ref="Megillah 3a:4">Ib.</cite> <he>ועוד בקש לגלות ת׳ של כתובים</he> and he wanted furthermore to reveal the rendition of the Hagiographa.

<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 13:2">Tosef. Sabb. XIII</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 14:2">XIV</cite>), 2; <cite ref="Shabbat 115a:7">Sabb. 115ᵃ</cite> <he>היו כתובין ת׳ וכ׳</he> if Scriptural books are written in Targum (Aramaic) or in any other language; <cite ref="Shabbat 115a:7">ib.</cite> <he>ובידו ספר איוב ת׳</he> and had in his hand the Book of Job in Targum. Ib.ᵇ <he>ת׳ שכתבו</he> … <he>שכתבו ת׳</he> Aramaic Biblical passages written in Hebrew translation, or Hebrew passages written in Aramaic. Ib. <he>ת׳ שבתורה</he> Aramaic words in the Pentateuch (Y’gar Sahădutha, <cite ref="Genesis 31:47">Gen. XXXI, 47</cite>).
<cite ref="Kiddushin 49a:11">Kidd. 49ᵃ</cite> <he>ת׳ דידן</he> our (the authorized Babylonian) Targum.
<cite ref="Mishnah Yadayim 4:5">Yad. IV, 5</cite> <he>ת׳ שבעזרא וכ׳</he> the Aramaic passages in Ezra &c.; a. fr.
